nodes.title: Part 1: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 1. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What command sets a file permission to rwxr-xr-- for owner, group, others?
flashcards.back: Octal permissions: owner(rwx=7), group(r-x=5), others(r--=4) = 754. chmod 754 file sets this. Alternatively: chmod u=rwx,g=rx,o=r file. Use ls -l to verify.

flashcards.front: How do you make a systemd service start automatically at boot?
flashcards.back: systemctl enable service: creates symlinks in /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/ so service starts at boot. systemctl enable --now service: enable AND start immediately. systemctl disable: remove autostart. systemctl is-enabled: check status.

flashcards.front: What command creates a logical volume of 5G named 'data' in VG 'vg0'?
flashcards.back: lvcreate -L 5G -n data vg0: -L size, -n name, vg0 is the volume group. After: mkfs.xfs /dev/vg0/data then mount. -l for LE units: -l 100%FREE uses all free space. lvs: list logical volumes.

flashcards.front: How do you persistently mount /dev/vg0/data to /mnt/data with xfs filesystem?
flashcards.back: /etc/fstab format: device mountpoint filesystem options dump pass. defaults = rw,suid,dev,exec,auto,nouser,async. 0 0 = no dump, no fsck. After editing: mount -a to test without reboot. Use blkid to get UUID for more reliable mounting.

flashcards.front: What command adds a user to the supplementary group 'wheel'?
flashcards.back: usermod -aG wheel username: -a (append, don't replace other groups), -G (supplementary group). Without -a: replaces ALL supplementary groups! gpasswd -a username wheel: alternative. id username: verify. User needs to re-login for group change to take effect (or: newgrp wheel in current session).

flashcards.front: How do you create a swap partition and enable it persistently?
flashcards.back: Steps: (1) fdisk/parted to create partition with type 82 (Linux swap). (2) mkswap /dev/sdb2. (3) swapon /dev/sdb2 (immediate). (4) /etc/fstab: '/dev/sdb2 swap swap defaults 0 0'. swapon -s: show active swap. free -h: memory + swap stats. swapfile: dd + mkswap + swapon works too. add to /etc/fstab

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of the /etc/hosts file and how does it interact with DNS?
flashcards.back: /etc/hosts: IP FQDN aliases per line. /etc/nsswitch.conf hosts: files dns — 'files' means check /etc/hosts first. For testing: add temporary entry. /etc/resolv.conf: DNS server configuration (nameserver IP, domain, search). hostnamectl: set system hostname. dnsdomainname: show domain. checked before DNS per /etc/nsswitch.conf

flashcards.front: How do you set the default target (runlevel equivalent) to multi-user (non-graph?
flashcards.back: systemctl set-default multi-user.target: non-graphical multi-user (like runlevel 3). graphical.target: desktop (runlevel 5). rescue.target: single-user maintenance. systemctl isolate multi-user.target: switch immediately (kills graphical). systemctl get-default: check current default target.

nodes.title: Part 3: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 3. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: How do you create a cron job that runs a script every weekday at 8am?
flashcards.back: Cron format: MIN HOUR DOM MON DOW COMMAND. 0 8 * * 1-5 = minute 0, hour 8, any day, any month, Mon-Fri (1-5). crontab -e: edit user crontab. Redirect output: 0 8 * * 1-5 /script >> /var/log/script.log 2>&1. Run as root: use /etc/crontab with user field.

flashcards.front: What command displays all listening TCP/UDP ports and the processes using them?
flashcards.back: ss -tulnp: -t TCP, -u UDP, -l listening, -n numeric (no name resolution), -p show process. Shows: port, state, PID, process name. Requires root for all PIDs. netstat -tulnp: older equivalent (net-tools package). lsof -i :80: what's using port 80. firewall-cmd --list-ports: what's open in firewall.

flashcards.front: How do you make a kernel parameter change persistent across reboots?
flashcards.back: Temporary: sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 (or echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward). Persistent: add 'net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1' to /etc/sysctl.conf or create /etc/sysctl.d/99-custom.conf. Apply without reboot: sysctl -p (reads /etc/sysctl.conf) or sysctl --system (reads all sysctl.d files).

flashcards.front: What is the difference between ps aux and ps -ef?
flashcards.back: ps aux: a=all users, u=user format, x=no terminal. Shows CPU%, MEM%, virtual/resident size. ps -ef: e=all processes, f=full format. Shows PPID (parent PID). Both useful: aux for resource usage, -ef for parent-child relationships. ps auxf: combined with process tree. ps -ef uses UNIX syntax showing PPID

pairs.stem: What is the difference between ps aux and ps -ef?
pairs.option: ps aux uses BSD syntax showing CPU/MEM%;.

nodes.title: Part 4: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 4. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: How do you configure virtual hosted websites in Apache (httpd)?
flashcards.back: VirtualHost: <VirtualHost *:80> ServerName www.example.com DocumentRoot /var/www/example ErrorLog /var/log/httpd/example-error.log </VirtualHost>. Each site: separate .conf in /etc/httpd/conf.d/. httpd -t: syntax check. systemctl reload httpd: apply. SELinux: chcon -Rt httpd_sys_content_t /var/www/example or use restorecon.

Journal management: journalctl --vacuum-size=500M (immediate cleanup). Persistent size limit: /etc/systemd/journald.conf → SystemMaxUse=500M → systemctl restart systemd-journald. journalctl --rotate: rotate log files. RuntimeMaxUse: volatile storage limit. Logs stored in /var/log/journal/ (persistent) or /run/log/journal/ (volatile).

flashcards.front: How do you create a Stratis storage pool and filesystem on RHEL 8+?
flashcards.back: Stratis: thin-provisioned storage with snapshots. Install: dnf install stratisd stratis-cli; systemctl enable --now stratisd. Create pool: stratis pool create mypool /dev/sdb. Create filesystem: stratis filesystem create mypool myfs. Mount: mount /stratis/mypool/myfs /mnt. List: stratis pool list; stratis filesystem list.

flashcards.front: What command creates a VDO (Virtual Data Optimizer) device on RHEL 8?
flashcards.back: VDO provides deduplication and compression. Install: dnf install vdo kmod-kvdo. Create: vdo create --name=myvdo --device=/dev/sdb --vdoLogicalSize=20G. Format: mkfs.xfs -K /dev/mapper/myvdo. Mount with discard: mount -o discard /dev/mapper/myvdo /mnt. vdostats --human-readable: check savings.
